name: South Lonak 2023
description: South Lonak Lake in Sikkim experienced a sudden breach on October 4, 2023, triggered by seismic moraine weakening and high monsoon precipitation. The flood destroyed the Chungthang Dam and downstream bridges, causing 55 deaths and over $120 million in infrastructure damage.

name: Bhote Koshi 2025
description: In July 2025, the Bhote Koshi glacial lake breached after extreme 3-day precipitation. The outburst destroyed four downstream hydropower facilities, cutting 8% of Nepal's total electrical grid capacity, resulting in over $200 million in losses but no deaths due to early visual warning.

name: Thame 2024
description: On August 16, 2024, a glacial lake above Thame village in Solukhumbu, Nepal, breached due to an ice avalanche sliding into the lake, causing moraine dam failure. The GLOF destroyed half of Thame village, including schools and lodges, with damages estimated at $15 million.

name: Dig Tsho 1985
description: The Dig Tsho GLOF occurred on August 4, 1985, in the Khumbu region of Nepal. An ice avalanche from the Langmoche glacier fell into the lake, causing a 5-meter surge that breached the moraine dam. The flood destroyed the newly built Namche Hydropower plant, 14 bridges, and farmland.

name: Tsho Rolpa 1998
trigger: high meltwater and structural moraine pressure
description: Tsho Rolpa is one of the largest glacial lakes in Nepal. In 1998, structural moraine pressure and accelerated melting led to extreme risk of outburst. Early siphoning and warning system installation mitigated the threat, preventing an imminent GLOF that threatened 20 downstream villages.

name: Chorabari Lake 2013
description: Chorabari Lake GLOF occurred on June 17, 2013, in Kedarnath, India, triggered by a massive cloudburst and a landslide falling into the lake. The resulting outburst destroyed Kedarnath town and downstream villages, causing over 5,000 deaths and massive economic damage.

name: Tam Pokhari 1998
description: Tam Pokhari GLOF occurred on September 3, 1998, in the Mount Everest region, triggered by an ice avalanche causing a breach of the moraine dam. The GLOF destroyed roads, bridges, and agricultural lands up to 80km downstream.

name: Lower Barun 2021
description: Lower Barun glacial lake experienced a minor outburst flood in 2021 due to progressive moraine piping and high summer melting. The warning allowed downstream hydropower projects to open gates, preventing casualties and limiting infrastructure damage.

name: Gelhaipuco 1964
description: Gelhaipuco lake in Tibet GLOF occurred in 1964 due to an ice avalanche falling into the lake, creating large waves that breached the moraine dam. It destroyed downstream farmland and bridges in the Arun river basin.

name: Luggye Lake 1994
description: Luggye Lake in Bhutan breached on October 7, 1994, due to an ice avalanche from the glaciers above. The outburst caused major damage to the downstream Punakha Dzong and farmland, claiming 21 lives.
